title: I Recorded the Laundromat Out-of-Order Card That Moved Every Hour

parts.text: I put eight dollars into washer 4 at 7:02 p.m. It died at 7:11. The owner slapped an OUT OF ORDER card on it and told me I had lost the cycle. I was thirty-two, holding wet jeans. An hour later the card was on washer 7, which a tourist was about to feed. Washer 4 was running for someone else. I filmed the card's journey on time-lapse from a folding table. Then the owner told me filming was banned because of other customers' laundry.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is banning the time-lapse of his traveling card while washer 4 takes a stranger's quarters.

social.video_title: The out-of-order card toured the machines that still worked — Part 1/2
social.description: Dead cycle, wet jeans, a card with legs. Then a filming ban. Would you have demanded a refund?

parts.text: The wall already had a camera the owner installed. I asked for my eight dollars and showed the time-lapse. He refunded in quarters that smelled like metal and spite. I moved to the place two blocks over. I posted the time-lapse on the neighborhood board without his face. The card cannot walk as far now. Wet jeans dried. Other customers' laundry remained unfilmed. Machines were the actors.

social.video_title: His own wall camera made the filming ban look shy — Part 2/2
social.description: Quarters back, new place, neighborhood board. Was a card a refund policy?
